question: 3 years ago, the age of a father was 21 years more than twice his son's age. After how many years, from now, will he be twice his son's age?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The age difference between two people remains constant forever.

Let Son's age 3 years ago be x, then Father's age was 2x + 21, making the difference x + 21.

When Father becomes twice the Son's age, the Son's age must exactly equal this difference (x + 21).

Presently, Son's age is x + 3. Hence, years required from now = (x + 21) − (x + 3) = 18.

**∴ The correct answer is 18 years.**
